newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Persson sees stability pact signing in Amsterdam.
newsitem.headline: Persson sees stability pact signing in Amsterdam.

text.p: Swedish Prime Minister Goran Persson said on Tuesday he expected the stability pact to be signed at a European Union summit in Amsterdam on June 16-17 but added there could be some delay.
He also said he expected Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU) to start according to plan on January 1, 1999.
When asked whether the stability pact would be signed in Amsterdam next week, he said:
"Yes, I think so but you never know. There could possibly be a short delay but I think it will be finalised in Amsterdam."
Persson was talking to reporters after speaking at a congress of the white collar union, TCO.
Regarding EMU, he said: "Yes, I think it will start on time."
Persson said France's call for an addition to the stability pact was predictable and added he did not have any objections.
"Sweden has long called for EU to fight unemployment," he said. "We don't have any problems with France including that discussion on the stability pact."
But such a discussion could lead to a more supranational union, he said.
"The Swedish people definitely oppose a federation. We have not had a referendum about a federation," he said, referring to the referendum on EU membership in 1994.
